subject: pe
title: Catastrophe Theory
welcome_lead: Hardy and Fazey — when cognitive anxiety meets high arousal, performance crashes.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on catastrophe theory of performance.
final_note: Catastrophe theory adds the missing element: high cognitive anxiety can collapse performance suddenly.

concepts.def: Hardy & Fazey 1987: high cognitive anxiety + high arousal → sudden performance drop.
Worry and negative thoughts; not the same as physiological arousal.
Performance does not return smoothly; requires arousal drop and re-focus.
Cognitive anxiety × somatic anxiety × performance — predicts cliff edge.
Sudden performance breakdown under pressure, often catastrophe-like.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hardy & Fazey extended inverted-U by adding cognitive anxiety — high values cause sudden cliff falls.
Low cognitive anxiety: smooth inverted-U. High cognitive anxiety: cliff-like drop above the peak.
Psychological skills training — imagery, self-talk, breathing — keeps cognitive anxiety manageable.

mcqs.q: Catastrophe theory predicts sudden performance drop when:
options: Cognitive anxiety AND arousal are both high

mcqs.q: In catastrophe theory, recovery from the drop:
options: Requires major drop in arousal and re-focus
